title: Software engineer
summary: Designs, builds, and maintains software systems — products people use, or the infrastructure underneath them.
dayInLife: Mornings in a codebase: reading, writing, reviewing. Afternoons in design discussions, debugging, and shipping small, testable changes. Deep work is the job; meetings are the tax.
education: A CS degree helps, but strong portfolios, internships, and bootcamps are common. The field rewards demonstrated skill.

title: Data scientist
summary: Turns messy data into decisions — models, experiments, and stories that change what an organization does next.
dayInLife: Cleaning data, testing hypotheses, building models, and translating findings for people who do not speak statistics. The craft is half math, half judgment.
education: Often a quantitative degree (stats, CS, econ, science). Graduate study is common but not required if the portfolio is strong.

title: UX designer
summary: Shapes how people experience a product — research, flows, prototypes, and the quiet decisions that make software feel obvious.
dayInLife: Interviews and usability tests, then sketches, Figma files, and critiques with engineers and PMs. Empathy is a method, not a mood.
education: Design, HCI, or psychology backgrounds are common. Bootcamps and strong case-study portfolios open doors.

title: Product manager
summary: Owns what gets built and why — the intersection of user need, business goal, and what the team can actually ship.
dayInLife: Writing problem statements, sequencing a roadmap, unblocking engineers, and saying no more often than yes. Influence without authority is the skill.
education: No single degree. Many come from engineering, design, consulting, or the field the product serves.

title: Cybersecurity analyst
summary: Protects systems and people from digital harm — monitoring, investigating, and hardening the places attackers look first.
dayInLife: Alerts, logs, threat reports, and careful incident response. Some days are quiet watchfulness; others are a race against a live attack.
education: IT, CS, or related degrees plus certifications (Security+, CySA+, later CISSP). Labs and CTFs matter.

title: Registered nurse
summary: Provides skilled, continuous care — assessment, treatment, advocacy, and the human presence that hospitals actually run on.
dayInLife: Shift work: vitals, meds, care plans, family conversations, and rapid judgment when a patient turns. Physical and emotional stamina are part of the craft.
education: Associate or bachelor of science in nursing, then licensure (NCLEX). BSN is increasingly preferred.

title: Clinical psychologist
summary: Assesses and treats mental and emotional life — therapy, testing, and the long work of helping people change patterns.
dayInLife: Sessions, notes, supervision, and the slow accumulation of trust. Research-informed, but the hour is always a relationship.
education: Doctoral degree (PhD or PsyD) and licensure. A long training path; master's-level counseling is a related, shorter route.

title: Physical therapist
summary: Restores movement and reduces pain — assessment, exercise, hands-on treatment, and coaching people through recovery.
dayInLife: A caseload of patients, each with a body and a story. You demonstrate, adjust, encourage, and document. Progress is visible.
education: Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) and licensure. A science-heavy undergraduate path helps.

title: K–12 teacher
summary: Designs learning for a room of young people — content, culture, and the daily practice of attention.
dayInLife: Lessons, feedback, parent notes, and the thousand micro-decisions of a classroom. Exhausting and, for the right person, the most alive work there is.
education: Bachelor's plus certification (varies by region). Subject-matter depth matters in secondary; pedagogy matters everywhere.

title: Instructional designer
summary: Builds learning that works at scale — courses, workshops, and digital programs for schools or companies.
dayInLife: Audience research, learning objectives, storyboards, and working with subject experts. You measure whether people actually learned.
education: Education, ID, or a field you teach, plus a portfolio of courses. Master's programs exist; many enter from teaching.

title: Research scientist
summary: Pushes the edge of what is known — experiments, papers, grants, and the patience of unanswered questions.
dayInLife: Lab or field work, analysis, writing, and the slow social world of peer review. Independence is high; feedback is delayed.
education: Usually a PhD in the field. Industry research roles sometimes hire strong master's graduates.

title: Management consultant
summary: Helps organizations solve messy, high-stakes problems — structure, evidence, and a recommendation they can act on.
dayInLife: Interviews, decks, analysis, and travel. You learn a new industry fast, then leave a plan behind. Intensity is the culture.
education: Often a strong bachelor's plus (later) an MBA. Case interviews matter more than the major.

title: Financial analyst
summary: Reads the numbers of a business or market and says what they mean for a decision — invest, cut, grow, wait.
dayInLife: Models, memos, earnings, and questions from people who need a clear answer by Friday. Precision under time pressure.
education: Finance, econ, accounting, or a quantitative field. CFA is a common later credential.

title: People / HR partner
summary: Designs how an organization hires, grows, and treats its people — the systems under culture.
dayInLife: Coaching managers, running processes (hiring, performance, conflict), and translating policy into something humans can use.
education: Psychology, business, or any field plus HR experience. SHRM or similar credentials help later.

title: Marketing manager
summary: Finds the people who need what you make and gives them a reason to care — brand, campaigns, and measurement.
dayInLife: Positioning, content, channels, budgets, and the argument about what the work is for. Mix of taste and analytics.
education: Any degree; portfolios and internships matter. Some come from writing, others from business or design.

title: Founder / entrepreneur
summary: Builds a venture from an unresolved need — product, customers, money, and the discomfort of no one else being in charge.
dayInLife: Whatever is on fire: selling, hiring, making, fundraising, or rewriting the plan. High autonomy, high variance.
education: No required degree. Domain skill plus the willingness to look foolish in public. Many found after another career.

title: Graphic designer
summary: Gives ideas a visible form — identity, layout, campaigns, and the visual language of a brand or publication.
dayInLife: Briefs, sketches, type, critique, and revisions. Software is the instrument; taste and constraint are the job.
education: Design school helps; a ruthless portfolio matters more. Self-taught paths are real if the work is.

title: Writer / content strategist
summary: Uses language as a tool — essays, scripts, product copy, or the information architecture of what a company says.
dayInLife: Research, drafts, edits, and the argument about audience. Some days are voice; some days are structure.
education: Any field that taught you to think on the page. Clips beat credentials.

title: Architect
summary: Designs buildings and the spaces between them — use, structure, light, and the long life of a place.
dayInLife: Drawings, models, codes, client meetings, and site visits. Beauty and regulation share the same desk.
education: Professional architecture degree (B.Arch or M.Arch) and licensure. A long, studio-heavy path.

title: Journalist
summary: Finds out what happened, why it matters, and says it clearly — reporting, interviewing, and public accountability.
dayInLife: Calls, documents, drafts against a clock. Curiosity with ethics. The industry is shifting; the craft is not optional.
education: Journalism or any rigorous writing field. Internships and published work matter most.

title: Environmental scientist
summary: Studies how people and ecosystems affect each other — field data, analysis, and advice that can change a policy or a site.
dayInLife: Sampling, GIS, reports, and time outdoors mixed with careful lab or desk work. The questions are local and planetary at once.
education: Environmental science, biology, chemistry, or geology. Master's common for specialist roles.

title: Urban planner
summary: Shapes how cities grow — land use, housing, transport, and the politics of who a place is for.
dayInLife: Maps, zoning, community meetings, and memos that have to survive a public hearing. Technical and civic in the same week.
education: Often a master's in urban planning (AICP later). Geography, architecture, or public policy are common undergrad paths.

title: Lawyer
summary: Advises and advocates inside a system of rules — contracts, disputes, regulation, or the defense of a person.
dayInLife: Reading, writing, negotiation, and (in some practices) court. Precision of language is a professional ethic.
education: Law degree and bar admission. A long, expensive path; practice area then defines the life.

title: Policy analyst
summary: Turns a public problem into options a government, think tank, or NGO can actually choose among.
dayInLife: Briefs, data, stakeholder calls, and the discipline of writing for people with ten minutes. Evidence plus politics.
education: Public policy, economics, law, or a domain (health, climate, education). Master's (MPP/MPA) is common.

title: Social worker
summary: Walks with people through systems that are often too hard to navigate alone — housing, health, family, crisis.
dayInLife: Visits, case notes, advocacy, and holding complexity without pretending you can fix it all. Boundaries are a skill.
education: BSW or MSW and licensure for clinical work. Field placements are the real training.

title: Nonprofit program director
summary: Runs the work of a mission — people, budget, programs, and the gap between a grant and a real outcome.
dayInLife: Staff, partners, reports to funders, and the constant translation of values into operations.
education: Any field plus proof you can run a program. Public admin, social work, or the cause area are common.

title: Electrician
summary: Installs and maintains the systems that make buildings work — power, safety, and the judgment of a licensed trade.
dayInLife: Job sites, prints, troubleshooting, and work you can point to at the end of the day. Apprenticeship is the school.
education: Apprenticeship (paid) plus licensure. No four-year degree required; mastery is years of supervised work.

title: Chef / culinary professional
summary: Runs a kitchen as both craft and operation — food, timing, people, and the standard you refuse to drop.
dayInLife: Prep, service, ordering, and leading a line. Physical, creative, and managerial in the same shift.
education: Culinary school is optional. Kitchens promote people who show up, taste, and take heat — literally.
